title: Direct native adoption removed a splice and improved a privileged-target diagnostic
summary: Correct-target prefetch initially showed no consistent latency benefit despite early transfer completion. Native publication of the staged physical blocks removed the second GPU prefix copy; a later lighter-logging demand comparison reached first token about 29 ms sooner in all three pairs.
scope: RTX 5080, Qwen2.5-1.5B BF16/TP1, one 2,048-token prefix, 56 MiB transfer and a privileged 750 ms correct-target lead. CPU integration preceded an old/adoption/old GPU check and then three balanced demand/adoption pairs.
limitations: A small oracle-style diagnostic, not deployable prediction or independent deployment samples. Background neutrality, capacity gains, other layouts and GPU cancellation/failure injection were not established. Pool occupancy fell from duplicate 112 MiB to one 56 MiB copy, not smaller preallocated VRAM.
decision: Retain exact identity, completion fences and native ownership as the mechanism. Keep this historical speculative-adoption result separate from the current CPU-only hint policy.

chart.caption: Three low-logging paired observations on one privileged-target workload. Negative is sooner; no confidence interval.
